title: All-order scalar causal extension and finite renormalization

items.title: Off-shell local polynomial scalar functionals
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and time orientation given by increasing $x^0$. A field configuration is any smooth real function $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$; it is off shell, meaning that it is not required to satisfy a field equation. For an integer $s\ge0$, its finite jet at $x$ is the finite tuple $j^s\phi(x)=(\partial^\alpha\phi(x))_{|\alpha|\le s}$, with multi-index derivatives in these coordinates.

An off-shell local polynomial scalar functional is a finite sum
$$F(\phi)=c+\sum_{a=1}^{N}\int_{\mathbb M} f_a(x)\,P_a(j^{s_a}\phi(x))\,d^4x,$$
where $c\in\mathbb C$, $f_a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$, each $P_a$ is a polynomial in the finitely many jet coordinates, and each $s_a$ is finite. Its support is contained in the compact set $\bigcup_{a=1}^{N}\operatorname{supp}f_a$. The collection of these functionals is denoted $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$. The involution is $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$. No physical units or field equation are imposed.

Precisely, $\operatorname{supp}F$ is the set of $x\in\mathbb M$ such that every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ contains the support of some $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$ for which $F(\phi+h)\ne F(\phi)$ for some smooth configuration $\phi$. It is closed and is contained in the displayed compact union, so it is compact. This definition is independent of the chosen finite presentation of $F$.

For $r\ge1$, define the $r$th functional derivative by
$$F^{(r)}(\phi)(h_1,\ldots,h_r)=\left.\frac{\partial^r}{\partial t_1\cdots\partial t_r}F\!\left(\phi+\sum_{j=1}^{r}t_jh_j\right)\right|_{t_1=\cdots=t_r=0},\qquad h_j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R).$$
The finite polynomial expansion makes this a symmetric multilinear form. Repeated integration by parts in each $h_j$ writes it as a compactly supported distribution kernel on the thin diagonal $\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in\mathbb M\}\subset\mathbb M^r$. Integrals use the fixed Minkowski density $d^4x$; all kernels are paired bilinearly with compactly supported smooth tests.

items.title: Local polynomial functionals are microcausal
items.statement:
For every $F\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$, every $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$ and every $r\ge1$, the kernel $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{WF}(F^{(r)}(\phi))\subseteq N^*\Delta_r\setminus0,$$
where $\Delta_r=\{(x,\ldots,x):x\in\mathbb M\}$ and
$$N^*\Delta_r=\{(x,\ldots,x;\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r):\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_r=0\}.$$
Consequently $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ avoids the all-future and all-past causal cotangent cones and $F$ belongs to $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$.

items.title: Local scalar time-ordered product contract
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ have metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and future direction given by increasing $x^0$. Use units $c=1$, so a mass parameter has inverse-length units. Define $x\in J^+(y)$ by $x^0-y^0\ge|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|$ and $x\in J^-(y)$ by $y^0-x^0\ge|\mathbf y-\mathbf x|$; for $A\subseteq\mathbb M$, put $J^\pm(A)=\bigcup_{y\in A}J^\pm(y)$. A field configuration is any smooth real function $\phi$; it is off shell because no field equation is imposed. The allowed local interactions are compactly supported finite polynomial functionals of $\phi$ and finitely many coordinate derivatives, integrated against $d^4x$. The support of a functional $F$ is the closed set of points each of whose neighborhoods contains the support of a compactly supported variation that changes $F$ for some configuration.

For $\Lambda\in SO^+(1,3)$, require $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the chosen future cone; $SO^+(1,3)$ denotes this identity component. The proper orthochronous Poincare group consists of $\gamma=(a,\Lambda)$ with $a\in\mathbb M$ and $\Lambda\in SO^+(1,3)$. It acts by $(\gamma\cdot\phi)(x)=\phi(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a))$ and $(\gamma\cdot F)(\phi)=F(\gamma^{-1}\cdot\phi)$.

For a distribution on a coordinate chart, its wavefront set consists of the nonzero cotangent directions where every compact localization fails to have a rapidly decreasing Fourier transform in every conic neighborhood. Covectors are future or past causal when their metric-dual vectors are causal with the indicated time orientation; a nonzero causal covector has a nonzero time component. Write $\Delta=\{(x,x):x\in\mathbb M\}$ and $N^*\Delta=\{(x,\xi;x,-\xi):\xi\ne0\}$. Write $(x,\xi)\sim(y,\eta)$ when $x,y$ lie on one null straight segment (a zero-length segment is allowed), and parallel transport along that segment carries $\xi$ to $\eta$. A fixed free scalar input consists of $m\ge0$, a two-point distribution $W$ satisfying
$$P_xW=P_yW=0,\qquad P=-\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b+m^2,$$
and the positive-frequency null wavefront condition
$$\operatorname{WF}(W)=\mathcal C^+:=\{(x,\xi;y,-\eta):(x,\xi)\sim(y,\eta),\ \xi\text{ future null}\}.$$
For a two-point distribution $U$, set $U^{\mathsf T}(x,y)=U(y,x)$ and let $U^*$ be complex conjugation. Assume $W$ is invariant under translations and $SO^+(1,3)$, satisfies $W-W^{\mathsf T}=iE$ for a fixed distribution $E$ supported where $x-y$ is causal, and satisfies $W^*=W^{\mathsf T}$.

The prescribed scalar time-ordered contraction input is a symmetric distribution $H_F\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb M^2)$ invariant under translations and $SO^+(1,3)$, equal to $W(x,y)$ on the open set $x^0>y^0$ and to $W(y,x)$ on $y^0>x^0$. The two prescriptions agree on spacelike-separated open supports because $E$ is supported on causal pairs. Translation invariance gives $H_F(x,y)=h_F(x-y)$ and $W(x,y)=w(x-y)$. For a distribution $T$ on $\mathbb R^4$, set $T_\rho(\varphi)=\rho^{-4}T(\varphi(\cdot/\rho))$ and define $\operatorname{sd}_0(T)$ as the infimum of real $\omega$ for which $\rho^\omega T_\rho\to0$ on each fixed test as $\rho\downarrow0$. Require $\operatorname{sd}_0(h_F),\operatorname{sd}_0(w)\le2$ and
$$\operatorname{WF}(H_F)\subseteq\Gamma_F:=N^*\Delta\cup\{(x,\xi;y,-\eta):x\ne y,\ (x,\xi)\sim(y,\eta),\ \xi\text{ future null if }x\in J^+(y),\ \xi\text{ past null if }x\in J^-(y)\}.$$
This is fixed conditional data: it does not claim existence of $W$ or $H_F$, and it does not define any singular restriction or product of $H_F$ on a diagonal.

For $r\ge1$, $F^{(r)}(\phi)$ denotes the distribution kernel on $\mathbb M^r$ of the mixed variation in $r$ compactly supported smooth directions, and set $F^{(0)}(\phi)=F(\phi)$. Define $\deg F$ as the largest positive $r$ with $F^{(r)}\ne0$, or $0$ if all positive-order derivative kernels vanish; in particular $\deg0=0$. The class $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)$ consists of finite polynomial functionals with compactly supported derivative kernels such that every nonzero wavefront tuple of each derivative kernel avoids both the cone of tuples whose entries are all future causal and the cone of tuples whose entries are all past causal; zero entries in either cone are allowed. For $F,G$ in this class, define
$$F\star_WG=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(\deg F,\deg G)}\frac{\hbar^r}{r!}\left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(r)}(\phi),W^{\otimes r}\right\rangle,$$
using distribution products and pushforwards under the stated wavefront transversality conditions, with the $r=0$ pairing interpreted as the pointwise product $F(\phi)G(\phi)$. Here $\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate, and Countable Choice is assumed for the supplier theorem defining these contractions.

A scalar time-ordered system is a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps
$$T_n:\big(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)\big)^n\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathbb M)\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket,\qquad T_0=1,\quad T_1=\operatorname{id}.$$
For $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ put $S_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{supp}F_i$ and $F_I=(F_i)_{i\in I}$. Causal factorization requires
$$T_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)=T_{|I|}(F_I)\star_W T_{|I^c|}(F_{I^c})$$
for every nonempty proper $I$ such that $S_I\cap J^-(S_{I^c})=\varnothing$; an empty block is the unit.

Field independence means that each numerical graph distribution is independent of the background field $\phi$; all $\phi$-dependence enters through the vertex kernels $F_i^{(r)}(\phi)$. In the graph expansion of $T_n$, vertices are labeled by $1,\ldots,n$ and an edge between distinct vertices contracts one derivative slot at each endpoint by $H_F$. A graph is a finite loopless multigraph, so parallel edges are allowed; if $r_{ij}$ edges join vertices $i$ and $j$, the Wick coefficient for that choice includes $\hbar^{\sum_{i<j}r_{ij}}/\prod_{i<j}r_{ij}!$. Finite-order local jet derivatives may act on incident edge kernels. Each coefficient is a finite sum of such contractions, since every input has finite polynomial degree. No graph term uses a singular product at a diagonal before extension.

For $n\ge2$, use relative coordinates $z_i=x_i-x_n$ ($1\le i<n$), so the total diagonal corresponds to $0\in\mathbb R^{4(n-1)}$. The relative scaling degree $\delta_\Gamma$ of a numerical graph distribution is defined by the same positive-dilation rule above in this relative dimension. The scaling condition requires each graph distribution on the punctured relative space, after its proper partial diagonals have been extended at lower vertex orders, to have a finite degree $\delta_\Gamma$, and each total-diagonal extension to retain that degree. Any two such extensions differ by derivatives $\partial^\beta\delta_0$ of order $|\beta|\le\lfloor\delta_\Gamma-4(n-1)\rfloor$ when $\delta_\Gamma\ge4(n-1)$, and agree when $\delta_\Gamma<4(n-1)$.

Covariance requires $T_n(\gamma\cdot F_1,\ldots,\gamma\cdot F_n)=\gamma\cdot T_n(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ for each proper orthochronous Poincare transformation. Fix the Lorentz Lie-algebra convention $[J_i,J_j]=\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$, $[J_i,K_j]=\epsilon_{ijk}K_j$, and $[K_i,K_j]=-\epsilon_{ijk}J_i$. For a formal coupling $g$, define coefficientwise
$$\mathcal S_g(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(ig/\hbar)^n}{n!}T_n(V,\ldots,V).$$
The anti-time-ordered series is $\overline{\mathcal S}_g(V):=\mathcal S_g(V)^*$, where the involution conjugates scalar coefficients, fixes real $g,\hbar$, and reverses the order of factors; $W^*=W^{\mathsf T}$ gives $(F\star_WG)^*=G^*\star_WF^*$. Formal unitarity requires $\overline{\mathcal S}_g(V)\star_W\mathcal S_g(V)=1$ for every real $V=V^*$. At each $g$-order, coefficients are finite Laurent polynomials in $\hbar$ before cancellation and are compared algebraically; there is no analytic convergence, positivity of formal coefficients, adiabatic limit, or gauge/Ward identity in this contract.

items.title: Finite scalar graphs have finite scaling degree
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and fix admissible scalar free data as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. In addition assume the following product-scaling bound (PB): whenever two finite-scaling-degree distributions $u,v$ on one resolved causal stratum have a wavefront-transversal product, their product has finite relative scaling degree and
$$\operatorname{sd}_0(uv)\le\operatorname{sd}_0(u)+\operatorname{sd}_0(v).$$
Assume (PB) at every successive product of edge pullbacks and lower-order local counterterms used below. Fix a finite loopless multigraph $\Gamma$ with $n\ge2$ labeled vertices, parallel edges allowed, and a finite multi-index derivative $\alpha_e$ on each edge $e$. Suppose every proper partial-diagonal subgraph has already received an extension of finite scaling degree by induction on its number of vertices. Then the numerical graph distribution on the complement of the total diagonal has finite scaling degree in the $4(n-1)$ relative coordinates. For a primitive graph, with no proper divergent subgraph, the bound is
$$\operatorname{sd}_0(t_\Gamma)\le 2|E(\Gamma)|+\sum_{e\in E(\Gamma)}|\alpha_e|.$$
For a graph with proper subgraphs, the same induction gives a finite bound obtained from this edge estimate and the finitely many derivative orders of its lower-order local counterterms.

items.title: Scalar Epstein–Glaser induction at finite perturbative order
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix any admissible flat scalar free datum and local scalar polynomial class as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. Also assume the graphwise product-scaling bound (PB) from [A2] below at every successive product of edge pullbacks and lower-order local counterterms. Then there exists a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps $T_n$ satisfying that contract at every finite perturbative order. At order $n$, each numerical graph distribution extends across the total diagonal in the $4(n-1)$ relative coordinates with its finite scaling degree; its extension ambiguity is a finite linear combination of derivatives of the diagonal delta distribution, of order at most $\lfloor\delta_\Gamma-4(n-1)\rfloor$ when $\delta_\Gamma\ge4(n-1)$ and zero when $\delta_\Gamma<4(n-1)$. Thus the coefficients form a formal series only; no convergence in the coupling, adiabatic limit, positivity claim, or gauge/Ward identity is asserted.

items.title: Renormalization maps form a formal composition group
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and the graphwise product-scaling bound (PB) in [A2] for the common free data. For two scalar time-ordered systems $T$ and $T'$ satisfying the local scalar contract for the same free data and with $T_0=T'_0=1$, $T_1=T'_1=\operatorname{id}$, define their normalized formal S-maps by
$$\mathcal S(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T_n(V,\ldots,V),\qquad \mathcal S'(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T'_n(V,\ldots,V).$$
There is a unique formal map $Z(V)=V+O(V^2)$ from local polynomial functionals to local polynomial functionals such that $Z(0)=0$, $dZ_0=\operatorname{id}$, $Z$ preserves supports and scalar Poincare covariance, and
$$\mathcal S'(V)=\mathcal S(Z(V))$$
coefficientwise. Such maps compose, and each has a recursively defined formal inverse; hence they form a group under composition.
